26.0.s.en: (1) Jeremiah's sermon in the temple and his arrest

26.0.0.en: After the death of the righteous King Josiah, his son Jehoahaz reigned a few months and was then carried captive to Egypt, and his brother Jehoiakim reigned in 609 BC. He had to pay a heavy tribute to Necho, Pharaoh of Egypt, yet he did not repent and fear God but was concerned to gather money to build a great palace for himself, and he opposed Jeremiah the prophet. So at the beginning of his reign, when his evil appeared, God commanded Jeremiah to stand in the house of the Lord, where many gather, to declare this prophecy, since the inhabitants of Jerusalem and all Judea come to the house of the Lord; and He emphasized to him that he must not diminish a word of the word of God, which shows the importance of this prophecy. Note that in this chapter and the following three chapters Jeremiah addresses his words to the people, the priests, the false prophets and the rulers, to call them to repentance.

26.1.0.en: God's purpose in the warning that comes in this prophecy is not vengeance on His children but to alert them to repent, so that He may forgive them all their sins.

26.2.0.en: God warns them and cautions them of woes that will come upon them if they do not obey His commandments.

26.3.0.en: God declares His word through His prophets, but sadly the people rejected their word.

26.4.0.en: Shiloh: the place where the tabernacle of meeting and the ark of the covenant of God were in the days of Samuel the prophet; the Philistines destroyed this city and seized the ark of the covenant of God from the children of Israel. God reminds them that He allowed the enemies to demolish the place of His house at Shiloh, and now He will allow the demolition of His temple in Jerusalem and her destruction if they do not repent, return to Him and obey His commandments.

26.5.0.en: The Holy Bible affirms that the words of this prophecy were heard by the people with their various leaders, the priests and the false prophets.

26.5.1.en: Do not rely on the outward forms of your spiritual life, as the Jews anciently relied on having the temple and Jerusalem, the city of God. All outward forms of piety are of no benefit without living their depths and without repentance.

26.6.0.en: After Jeremiah declared this prophecy, all the people, led by the priests and the false prophets, rose against him and seized him to kill him because of his prophecy about the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple. It was an uprising of the whole people against Jeremiah.

26.7.s.en: (2) Jeremiah warns the princes against shedding his blood

26.7.0.en: The princes of Judah: he means the judges and civil rulers responsible for leading the people. When the princes of Judah, who helped the king in governing the kingdom, heard all of Jeremiah's prophecy about the destruction of the temple and Jerusalem, they were greatly troubled. They went up from the royal palace, where they do their work of administering the affairs of the kingdom, to the temple of God, because it is built on a hill, and gathered at one of its gates, called "the new gate," to try Jeremiah, as was the ancient custom of holding trials at the gates and squares of cities so as to have room for the crowds to gather and follow the trial (Gen 23:10-20) (Ruth 4:1).

26.8.0.en: When the judges and princes reached the gate of the house of the Lord, the priests and the false prophets hurried to them, holding Jeremiah, and repeated to them what he had said in his prophecy about the destruction of the house of the Lord, and announced the verdict before the trial: the necessity of putting him to death. This shows their evil and their unwillingness to examine matters, because they hated Jeremiah on account of his earlier prophecies against them.

26.9.0.en: Jeremiah affirmed before the princes and all the people that he is a prophet sent by God to declare the prophecies they hear; therefore they must obey the words of this prophecy.

26.10.0.en: Jeremiah summed up what was required of his hearers: repentance and return to God, and the amendment of their faults, that is, leaving their lusts and their worship of idols. Then God would forgive them all their sins and turn back from the punishment He had decreed against them, namely the destruction of Jerusalem.

26.11.0.en: Jeremiah was not afraid of the threat to kill him, and declared his readiness to die for God's sake, saying that it was in their power to put him to death.

26.11.1.en: Do not fear the threats of the wicked, and trust in God's protection of you. Then you will proclaim the voice of God and live faithfully, confident that evil has no authority over you unless God permits it for your benefit; and He will be with you and support you in all your afflictions.

26.12.0.en: Jeremiah warned them against killing him, for by this they would fall into the sin of killing without cause that a man deserves, and God would be angrier with them and with their city because of the shedding of his innocent blood.

26.13.s.en: (3) The princes against the priests and the prophets

26.13.0.en: God intervened and convinced the princes of Jeremiah's innocence, and that he is a prophet sent by God who fulfilled his mission and intends no personal evil against Jerusalem. Thus they turned away from the hatred of the priests and the false prophets, and rejected their mistaken counsel which wanted to put Jeremiah to death.

26.14.0.en: God also sent the elders and heads of the people, that is, the foremost of the people at hand, and they supported the words of the judges and princes in the king's palace against the priests and the prophets by reminding them of ancient events that support Jeremiah's innocence and his rescue from death.

26.15.0.en: Plowed: tilled with the plow, that is, demolished and leveled with the ground.

26.15.1.en: The high places of a forest: hills of ruined buildings like the hills found in the wilderness. The elders reminded the judges, the priests and all the assembled people of what happened about a century earlier, when a prophet named Micah the Morasthite, that is, from a town called Moresheth, arose and prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem and her complete ruin (Mic 3:12).

26.16.0.en: King Hezekiah, who was reigning at that time, did not become angry and take vengeance on Micah by killing or torturing him; on the contrary, he feared God and offered repentance, he and his people (2 Kgs 18:14), so God forgave them and postponed carrying out the destruction of Jerusalem. Consequently, taking vengeance on Jeremiah and killing him would cast the whole people into a great sin, because by this they would be resisting God.

26.16.1.en: God is able to rescue you at the right time, however much enemies rise against you and however great their strength. So do not be terrified of them: He sends you help in due time from where you do not know. God is with you, so do not fear any man.

26.17.0.en: Kirjath-jearim: a city of the Gibeonites lying northwest of Jerusalem at a distance of eight miles.

26.17.1.en: Jeremiah tells us a story that shows how fierce King Jehoiakim was and how he was led along behind the priests and the false prophets. It happened at the same time that a prophet of God arose in the village of Kirjath-jearim and prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem exactly as Jeremiah prophesied. God sent him, as He sent Jeremiah and, anciently, Micah, to confirm what would happen so that the Jews would repent and not rely on having the temple, for this is not enough for their salvation as long as they are in sin.

26.18.0.en: Jehoiakim and all his helpers were greatly angered, and made war on Urijah the prophet, and he commanded that he be killed, so he fled to Egypt.

26.19.0.en: There were treaties and an understanding between Jehoiakim king of Judah and Necho, Pharaoh of Egypt, so Jehoiakim sent men, and they seized Urijah in Egypt and brought him to Jehoiakim, who killed him and cast his body with contempt into the graves of the common people, and not with the honor given to prophets.

26.19.1.en: Do not persist in sin, insisting on it and trying to carry it out by every means, lest you bring upon yourself the wrath of God. He is long-suffering but at the same time just, so do not make light of His long-suffering.

26.20.0.en: Ahikam the son of Shaphan: one of Jehoiakim's helpers. His father Shaphan was one of Josiah's helpers and was godly and loved Jeremiah. The discussions were still heated, the priests on one side and the false prophets on the other, over killing Jeremiah or acquitting him. So God moved the heart of one of the godly, Ahikam, one of the king's helpers, and he interceded and confirmed the words of the judges, and so rescued Jeremiah from being put to death.

27.0.s.en: (1) Warnings to the neighboring kings in Jerusalem

27.0.0.en: Many think that King Jehoiakim is mentioned here by mistake and that the correct name is King Zedekiah. In the Arabic and Syriac translation the first verse reads: "Zedekiah reigned in place of Jehoiakim." This was in 597 BC. Babylon made this king reign in place of Jehoiachin, whom it carried captive to Babylon after he had reigned a few months. So at the beginning of Zedekiah's reign Jeremiah spoke this prophecy. In those days the kingdom of Babylon, only four years after its rise, faced wars in the east from Elam and unrest in Syria, so some kings west of the kingdom of Babylon, around Jerusalem, gathered and organized an alliance to resist Babylon. The false prophets in the kingdom of Judah affirmed that Babylon would collapse, and encouraged King Zedekiah and the kings allied with him to fight Babylon because it would fall and collapse. Only one person stood against all this current, demanding that the people submit to the bondage of Babylon, and he was Jeremiah the prophet, as the Lord commanded him.

27.1.0.en: Bonds: straps of leather or ropes tied around the neck of an animal.

27.1.1.en: Yokes: the plural of yoke, a piece of wood placed on the necks of two animals, tied with ropes or leather around the neck and fastened there; a crosswise beam is mounted on the yoke and draws at its end the farming implements such as the plow.

27.1.2.en: God asked Jeremiah to make yokes with ropes fastened to them and to put them on his neck as a visual aid by which he declares his submission to the king of Babylon, as an example before the messengers of the kings and before King Zedekiah, that they might submit to the king of Babylon.

27.1.3.en: Jeremiah bore the yoke, which signifies the bondage of sin, although he is a godly man far from evil. By this he is a type of Christ, who is without sin and bore the Cross for us to die in our place and redeem us.

27.2.0.en: Edom: the descendants of Esau, living in the mountains of Seir.

27.2.1.en: Moab: the descendants of Lot by his elder daughter.

27.2.2.en: The children of Ammon: the descendants of Lot by his younger daughter.

27.2.3.en: Tyre: a large commercial city on the coast of the Mediterranean in Lebanon.

27.2.4.en: Sidon: a city on the coast of the Mediterranean south of Tyre.

27.2.5.en: There were messengers from the countries of Edom, Moab, the children of Ammon, Tyre and Sidon who had come to King Zedekiah to ally with him against Babylon. He gave each of them a yoke to bind and carry to his king as a visual aid of the necessity of his submission to the king of Babylon, as an animal submits to the yoke placed on its neck.

27.3.0.en: God sent a message through Jeremiah, with the messengers of the kingdoms mentioned above, declaring in it that He is God, the Creator of the earth and of the man and beast upon it, that is, that He has complete authority, and gives the kingdom to whom He wills of mankind to carry out the will of God.

27.4.0.en: God continues His speech: He uses Nebuchadnezzar His servant to carry out His will by possessing all the lands of his kingdom, as an instrument to discipline His people and the other peoples for their disobedience and evils.

27.5.0.en: His son and his son's son: either he means his sons and grandsons, or he means his son Evil-merodach and his son's son Belshazzar (Dan 5:11). The time of his land: the time when the kingdom of Babylon collapses and the kingdom of the Medes and Persians rises against it. Many nations and great kings: the kings of the Medes and Persians who laid Babylon waste and took all their lands.

27.5.1.en: God declares that the peoples of the earth will submit not only to Nebuchadnezzar but also to those who succeed him from his seed up to his grandson Belshazzar, and this was for seventy years. After that the kingdom of the Medes and Persians arises, a union between two kingdoms, to enslave Babylon and take all its possessions and use them as it wishes.

27.6.0.en: God adds that whoever disobeys and resists the king of Babylon will die either by the sword, by disease, or by hunger, which is the opposite of all that the false prophets claimed.

27.7.0.en: Your prophets: he means the false prophets.

27.7.1.en: Your diviners: the plural of diviner, one who claims knowledge of the unseen in any form.

27.7.2.en: Your dreamers: one who claims to have dreams that tell him the future.

27.7.3.en: Your enchanters: the plural of enchanter, who likewise claims knowledge of the unseen.

27.7.4.en: Your sorcerers: the plural of sorcerer, who likewise claims, by the power of Satan, to know the future and to be able to work wonders.

27.7.5.en: God also forbids them to listen to those who claim prophecy and knowledge of the unseen, whether false prophets or others, and who prevent them from submitting to the king of Babylon and encourage them to resist him.

27.8.0.en: He also warned the peoples of these kingdoms that their believing the words of the false prophets would make the king of Babylon attack them, drive them out of their lands and destroy them, as God permitted him. It is remarkable that God says He will drive out these peoples; what is meant is that He will accomplish this by the hand of the king of Babylon.

27.9.0.en: On the contrary, God gives good news to whoever obeys His word and submits to the king of Babylon, that he will dwell in his land, do his work and be settled in his life.

27.9.1.en: Accept the word of God even if it is hard, such as keeping the difficult commandments, so that you may find your salvation, and do not be deceived by the words of the people of the world, which deceive you that sin gives you comfort and makes you succeed in life.

27.9.3.en: 12- I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live. 13- Why will ye die, thou and thy people, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as the LORD hath spoken against the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon? 14- Therefore hearken not unto the words of the prophets that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you. 15- For I have not sent them, saith the LORD, yet they prophesy a lie in my name; that I might drive you out, and that ye might perish, ye, and the prophets that prophesy unto you.

27.10.0.en: Jeremiah repeated the same words to King Zedekiah, to submit to the king of Babylon so that he and his people might live. This time he responded and left this alliance, but he returned and rebelled against the king of Babylon, relying on Egypt, so the king of Babylon seized him, killed his sons, and then put out his eyes.

27.11.0.en: He assured him that if he did not obey God and submit to the king of Babylon he would die by one of three means, namely the sword, disease or hunger.

27.12.0.en: He warned him against being influenced by the words of the false prophets, because they claim that God sent them while God is innocent of their words; they intend to lead you astray so that you are driven out of your land, you and also these prophets.

27.12.1.en: The children of God ought to hold fast to His commandments before the children of the world, and indeed be an example of obedience to God, so that they escape the evil of the world and are a model for others.

27.12.2.en: (3) Warning to the priests and the people (vv. 16-22).

27.12.3.en: 16- Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith the LORD; Hearken not to the words of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the LORD'S house shall now shortly be brought again from Babylon: for they prophesy a lie unto you.

27.12.4.en: 17- Hearken not unto them; serve the king of Babylon, and live: wherefore should this city be laid waste? 18- But if they be prophets, and if the word of the LORD be with them, let them now make intercession to the LORD of hosts, that the vessels which are left in the house of the LORD, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, go not to Babylon. 19- For thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this city, 20- Which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took not, when he carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem;

27.12.5.en: 21- Yea, thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that remain in the house of the LORD, and in the house of the king of Judah and of Jerusalem; 22- They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be until the day that I visit them, saith the LORD; then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place.

27.13.0.en: God exposes the lying of the false prophets who claim the collapse of Babylon and the return of the vessels of the house of the Lord that the king of Babylon had taken.

27.14.0.en: He calls them to obey the king of Babylon so that they do not die and Jerusalem is not destroyed. And Jeremiah, of course, is not an agent of Babylon, as the false prophets claim, but is the one speaking the word of God, that they may accept their discipline and so repent of their sins.

27.15.0.en: God gives proof of the lying of the false prophets: if they are sent by God, let them intercede with Him so that the rest of the vessels of the Lord and the contents of the temple which the king of Babylon had not taken may not go.

27.16.0.en: The pillars: the two bronze pillars which King Solomon made and set in the outer court (1 Kgs 7:15-22). The sea: it corresponds to the laver in the tabernacle of meeting, and its form is a round bronze basin about five meters in diameter in which water is placed for washing.

27.16.1.en: The bases: twelve bases, each in the form of an ox, made of bronze, on which rested the bronze sea mentioned above (1 Kgs 7:23-25). These parts of the temple, which are the pillars, the sea and its bases, and other contents of the temple, Nebuchadnezzar did not take when he carried captive Jeconiah, or King Jehoiachin, and the nobles who were in Babylon. So Jeremiah asks the false prophets to pray to God that they may not be taken to Babylon too, if they are truly real prophets; but what will actually happen is that they will be taken in the second attack of the king of Babylon on Jerusalem.

27.17.0.en: The day that I visit them: when Babylon collapses before the kingdom of the Medes and Persians and Cyrus the Persian king orders the return of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Jerusalem.

27.17.1.en: God declares that the rest of the contents of the temple will be taken by the king of Babylon and remain there until the end of the Babylonian kingdom and the rise of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, when everything will be returned to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.

27.17.2.en: God permits affliction for a temporary period so that you repent, and then He lifts it from you and restores to you all your glory. So do not be troubled by the affliction, but hasten to repentance and to holding fast to God.
